follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference: on rounded rows the tax benefit pushes kept profit to $14.00 per $100, vs $13.99 exact.
oneTimers: A one-time $457M tax benefit — a change in tax position on a historical transaction from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act transition period — turned $25M of pre-tax income into $482M of net income. Non-GAAP results exclude it through a $705M income-tax adjustment.
A $141M fair-value loss on convertible senior notes and capped calls acquired from CyberArk sits inside other expense; it is excluded from non-GAAP results and will swing with the share price.

Share-based compensation of $622M and amortization of acquired intangibles of $282M (vs $39M a year ago) are excluded from non-GAAP operating income — but stock pay dilutes shareholders, and the amortization will recur for years.

On the same day, Palo Alto signed a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5B in Palo Alto stock (per the 10-Q; no price was in the earnings release). It is not in this quarter's numbers.
otherDetail: Other expense of $71M, net — a $141M fair-value loss on convertible senior notes and capped calls acquired from CyberArk, partly offset by interest income on cash and investments.

segments.name: Subscription & support
segments.note: Security software subscriptions and support contracts — the recurring core, 83% of revenue; Next-Gen Security ARR grew 66% to $9.73B.

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Firewall hardware and appliances shipped to customers.

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 39% to $3.44B, Next-Gen Security ARR 66% to $9.73B, and remaining performance obligations 35% to $21.0B — and management raised full-year guidance materially. But GAAP operating profit fell 69%, and the tax line, not the business, produced the net-income growth.
takeaways.title: Record growth, messy profit

takeaways.text: Amortization of acquired intangibles jumped 7× to $282M, a $141M fair-value loss on CyberArk's convertible notes hit other income, and $95M of acquisition payments went out in cash. The test is whether CyberArk's identity-security revenue grows fast enough to justify the charges.
takeaways.title: CyberArk is now the story

takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow of $1.94B is 56% of revenue — even in a seasonally slow Q1, the subscription model throws off cash that funds the acquisition strategy without raising money.
takeaways.title: Cash generation is the quiet strength

verdict: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 39% to a record $3.44B and raised full-year guidance sharply, but GAAP operating profit fell 69% to $96M as the CyberArk acquisition flooded the income statement with amortization and stock compensation — and a one-time $457M tax benefit is what turned $25M of pre-tax profit into $482M of net income.
